svg.title: Forms & audiences
svg.desc: Article or guide: Article: headline, engaging opening, developed paragraphs and an ending with a purpose. Guide: organise around the reader’s needs. Action + how + why turns a tip into useful advice. Letter: State why you are writing, develop the case, finish with an appropriate request or conclusion. Named recipient: Yours sincerely. Unknown: Yours faithfully. Be firm and courteous; challenge ideas, not people. Speech or talk: Address listeners and use words that sound natural aloud. Signpost changes so listeners can follow. Short emphasis can follow a longer explanation. A talk is written speech, not a list of stage directions. Review: Detail + judgement + reason. Choose criteria such as accessibility, atmosphere, quality or value. Give strengths and limitations; recommend for a named type of reader. Avoid retelling the entire plot. Report or leaflet: Report: purpose → grouped findings → implications → recommendation if requested. Leaflet: clear sections with useful developed information. Headings help navigation; decoration does not replace content. Adapt the same idea: To a friend: warm and direct. To a headteacher: respectful, clear and specific. Keep the main purpose in view. Match details to what the reader can know, value and realistically do.
